skill.description: Generate and pre-score email subject lines and preheaders for spam-pattern flags, truncation, emoji use, and inbox preview clarity.

skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: All 53 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown links, backtick formatting, and ordinary workflow prose. The skill provides local, heuristic email subject-line guidance and contains no executable commands, network requests, arbitrary filesystem access, or prompt-injection attempt. Its documented memory write requires user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Static scanners may misclassify Markdown backticks and relative documentation links as command execution or path traversal.
remediation.suggestion: Keep references clearly labeled as documentation links and preserve the explicit user-confirmation requirement for optional memory writes.

remediation.issue: Heuristic spam and truncation checks can be mistaken for deliverability guarantees.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the existing labels that distinguish measured character counts from estimated heuristic results and direct full deliverability checks to the dedicated skill.

content.value_statement: Weak subject lines can waste email test cells and hide the main promise on mobile. This skill creates variants, checks practical risks, and ranks candidates before testing.
actual_capabilities: Generates three to eight subject line and matched preheader variants.
Labels each variant with a stable identifier and messaging angle.
Counts subject and preheader characters for desktop and mobile truncation review.
Flags heuristic spam patterns, emoji use, and misleading urgency.
Renders an inbox-style preview using the sender name, subject, and preheader.
Ranks variants and explains which candidates should advance to testing.
limitations: It provides heuristic flags, not a mailbox-provider spam or placement verdict.
It does not write email body copy, design experiments, or calculate statistical significance.
It cannot verify unsupported prices, discounts, statistics, or scarcity claims.
Rendering limits are practical estimates and may vary by email client and device.

use_cases.title: Prepare a promotion test
use_cases.description: Create and rank promotional subject lines before assigning test cells.

use_cases.title: Review outbound messaging
use_cases.description: Check B2B cold-outbound subjects for tone, truncation, and emoji concerns.

use_cases.title: Refine a newsletter send
use_cases.description: Compare newsletter subject and preheader pairs in an inbox-style preview.

prompt_templates.title: Score existing subjects
prompt_templates.prompt: Pre-score these subject lines for mobile truncation and spam-pattern flags. Use [Sender] as the from-name: [paste subjects].

prompt_templates.title: Generate promotion variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate five subject line and preheader pairs for [offer] in promo mode. Rank them by the heuristic pre-score.

prompt_templates.title: Compare inbox previews
prompt_templates.prompt: Show desktop and mobile inbox previews for these three subject and preheader pairs. Cut any variant that hides the main promise: [paste pairs].

prompt_templates.title: Use campaign context
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this past campaign export and this new offer, create six distinct subject-line angles. Label measured counts and estimated heuristic flags separately.

output_examples.input: Generate three promo subject lines for a summer course sale.
output: SUBJ-A | Benefit | Learn faster this summer | Preheader: Short lessons for your next skill.
SUBJ-B | Offer | Summer courses, now 20% off | Preheader: Explore the full course catalog.
Ranked shortlist: SUBJ-A first for a clear promise and clean mobile preview.

output_examples.input: Review a cold-outbound subject with an emoji.
output_examples.output: Flag: Emoji use in cold-outbound mode. Suggested revision: A faster way to prepare monthly reports. The revised subject removes the emoji and keeps the benefit visible early.

best_practices: Provide the audience, email mode, offer, and sender name before generating variants.
Use verified claims only and mark missing evidence before testing a subject line.
Treat the ranking as a pre-test screen, then validate winners with a controlled experiment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a clean heuristic check as an inbox-placement guarantee.
Do not use invented urgency, prices, discounts, or performance statistics.
Do not change multiple email variables when testing subject line candidates.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee inbox placement?
faq.answer: No. It provides heuristic subject and preheader checks only. Mailbox-provider placement requires separate deliverability review.

faq.question: Can it generate subject lines from an offer?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the offer, audience, mode, and sender name when available.

faq.question: What email modes does it support?
faq.answer: It supports promotional, cold-outbound, and newsletter workflows.

faq.question: Why are some results labeled estimated?
faq.answer: Spam-pattern and rendering limits are practical heuristics. Character counts are measured.

faq.question: Can it analyze past campaign exports?
faq.answer: Yes. You can provide an exported campaign list to inform angles and length preferences.

faq.question: Does it write the email body?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the subject line and preheader. Use a dedicated email-writing workflow for body copy.
